title: Prefill and batch fallthrough lab notes — weekly
content:
Context:
This was the weekly lab/standup for the Prefill & Batching effort. Goal for this sprint: reduce tail latency regressions when a cold KV segment receives a short burst of requests and ensure graceful fallthrough from prefill to on-demand micro-batching without causing tail spikes or over-eager GPU kernels.

Attendees: Marisol, Ravi, Elena, Sam, Jonah (SRE drop-in), Priya (observability).

Runbook snapshot (what we tested):
- Staircase windowing: change batch wait from fixed 4ms -> adaptive staircase: [1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms] up to 32ms depending on arrival rate.
- Fallthrough policy: if prefill miss and queue growth > 12 reqs in 5ms, allow immediate fallback to micro-batch with conservative KV shadowing.
- KV segment TTL fuzz: randomized TTL on shadow entries to avoid synchronized evictions for high-churn keys.
- Burst-damping gates: if a GPU is saturated (util > 0.88) for 10ms, throttle prefill and divert to CPU-prefill path (soft degrade).

Key observations (metrics from lab cluster):
- Latency: 95th reduced by 6% on synthetic chat workload when staircase windowing used vs baseline fixed 4ms. However, 99.9th percentile increased in one noisy run (+18ms).
- Throughput: marginal uptick in achieved throughput when fallthrough allowed; micro-batching path absorbed spikes better.
- GPU utilization: burst-damping gates prevented long sustained spikes, but introduced small oscillations (~5% util variance) when combined with TTL fuzz.
- Cold-key tail cases: two reproducible patterns that still cause >120ms spikes: (1) long context-prefill then immediate short followup (2) many small keys arriving interleaved causing eviction churn.

Hypotheses and quick experiments: 
1) Hypothesis: 99.9th spike caused by synchronous prefill completions hitting kernel handshake simultaneously.
   - Experiment: add jittered prefill completion acknowledgement (0-2ms) to smooth handshake. Result: single-run showed 9ms improvement on 99.9th. Need more runs.
2) Hypothesis: eviction churn from deterministic per-segment TTL causes burst evictions.
   - Experiment: TTL fuzz (±30%) reduced observed eviction storms in synthetic churn test.
3) Hypothesis: staircase window should adapt based on recent inter-arrival distribution, not absolute rate.
   - Experiment: quick POC that switches staircase tiers using EMA of inter-arrival (alpha=0.2). Observed faster convergence on steady-state for moderate burst patterns.

Action items (owners + due):
- Ravi: run 100-run noise-reduction A/B for jittered prefill ack; include 99.9/99.99 percentiles and kernel-level timing breakdown. Due 2026-12-14.
- Elena: instrument per-segment eviction histogram to find worst offenders by key-cardinality; push a Grafana panel to the prefill dashboard. Due 2026-12-10.
- Sam: add a microbenchmark that simulates interleaved small-key churn and log KV ops timings (PR draft: GH #2397). Due 2026-12-11.
- Marisol: draft fallback policy matrix (which path to choose when) and circulate to SRE for review. Due 2026-12-09.
- Priya: record a 10-minute runbook video for oncall explaining the burst-damping gate and how to flip overrides; upload to shared playbooks. Due 2026-12-13.

Notes / rough ideas to revisit:
- Consider a two-phase handoff where prefill primes a tiny prefix cache on CPU immediately and GPU prefill continues in background; this would reduce kernel handshake pressure for short followups.
- Explore a small-size dedup window (5ms) where identical prefill requests consolidate at the router layer before entering KV prefill queues. Could drastically reduce redundant prefill work for high-duplication workloads.
- For regulated customers (private deployments), make the fallthrough conservative: default to no CPU-prefill path unless explicitly enabled in config. Add a flag in console.

Open blockers/questions:
- Need clarity on acceptable micro-batching latency SLO when fallthrough engaged; product to weigh in (tagging product-hosted-api).
- Is the jittered-ack approach safe for metrics aggregation? Might create small noise in per-request traces; SRE to confirm.

Incidental:
- Found an unrelated GH flaky test (serving-runtime/tests/test_kv_eviction.py) failing under heavy parallelism; opened PR to increase test isolation (link above).
- Noted that the Linear ticket INF-417 has been re-prioritized; align action items once updated.

Follow-up meeting: next lab sync Tuesday 2026-12-14 10:30 PST. Please bring A/B results or updated dashboards.

Notes-to-self (quick scribbles):
- Try increasing handshake backoff only for cold-key trajectories (detect via last-seen timestamp > 10s).
- If micro-batch path is taking >4x the tokens-per-req of prefill path, consider soft quota per-client to avoid abuse.

Appendix (quick benchmark numbers from today's run, median of 5 runs):
- Baseline fixed-4ms: p50=12.1ms p95=28.3ms p99=45.0ms p99.9=92.1ms
- Staircase adaptive: p50=11.8ms p95=26.6ms p99=42.3ms p99.9=86.4ms
- Staircase + jittered-ack (single run): p99.9=77.0ms
summary: Weekly lab/standup notes for the prefill and batching fallthrough project. Staircase windowing + fallthrough policy experiments showed p95 improvements but occasional p99.9 spikes; action items assigned for instrumentation, A/B runs, and a fallback policy write-up.
